column1: # Technical terms as they are spoken: exact written form (case matters)<TAB>the words to say.
# Applied before the text rules (dizione) and the word list, as a lookup, never a guess: add a term
# after hearing it come out wrong. A run of capitals is spelled (AWS); keep it joined, since a lone A or I reads as a word.
# Acronyms said letter by letter (Tim, 16 Nov: "VLLM, like each letter spoken"). A plural spells its
# letters apart, since a joined run with an s reads as a word ("LLMs" came out "lelms").
# Spaced, since run together they were misheard (STT as "SDT", CLI as "cla"); ONNX is said "onyx".
# Weekdays and model sizes (the open-release worker, 16 Nov). One file for lalala and the release.
# A word a camelCase name splits into ("getUserById").
# Dotfiles (the open-release worker, 16 Nov). ".env" alone as "dot en vee": "dot env" was heard ".end" (M3,
# f13, e21); the longer forms keep "dot env", which every voice reads clearly there.
# Tim, 16 Nov: MLX and SGLang were said wrong, and "the beta lead is" read "lead" as the metal.
# Tim, 16-17 Nov: JS is "J S"; ".js" also as a suffix, said without the dot (Node.js = "Node J S", Transformers.js, main.js).
# Tim, 16 Nov: CLI still sounded wrong. "C L I" ended on an unstressed "I"; "eye" carries the stress.
# Tech terms, 18 Nov ("GGUF" was said as "just"): software, ML/AI and robotics, case-aware (only these exact forms, so
# rag, slam, pid stay words). Spelled letters are spaced: joined runs blurred. Checked by Whisper on nano and tiny.
